name: THE BOARDING HOUSE
materialIdentity: Patterned wallpaper, a plank floor and a proper rug, a coal fire and two lamps: warm (errata 183)

entrances.note: In at the front door, from the map.

LOOK_AT.say: A queen, in an oval frame, looking down on the parlor as if she owned the boarding house. She may.
repeat: A print of a painting of a queen, framed, and dusted on top of the frame. That is real devotion.
She hangs straight. In Consolation that makes her the most upright thing for miles.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. She is not amused, and she is not going to say so twice.
repeat: Nothing. Her expression suggests silence is expected.
The wire behind the frame, ticking against its nail as the fire warms the wall.

LOOK_AT.say: Lace, on every chair, four hundred miles from anywhere.
repeat: Every chair has one, and every one is starched. Two women in a mining camp starch lace. I'd follow them into battle.
Somebody has darned one, so neatly I only found it by looking for a flaw. There's always one.
then: Somebody carried these here on purpose.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. This is the quietest room in the territory.
repeat: Nothing. Not even the chairs creak. They wouldn't dare.
Nothing. This room is quiet on purpose, and it works.

LOOK_AT.say: A china pot, cups and a sugar bowl with tongs. Tongs. In Consolation.
repeat: The cups are a set. Every one of them matches. I have not seen two things match in this town since I arrived.
A tea cosy on the pot, knitted, in the shape of a hen. I have never respected a hen so much.

LISTEN_TO.say: A spoon turning in a cup, and then stopping, because I am being looked at.
repeat: The pot ticking as it cools.
Nothing. The cups wait in their saucers like guests who know their place.

overrides.PICK_UP: Not without being asked. And I can tell already that I will not be asked.

LOOK_AT.say: An upright with its lid shut and a doily on top.
repeat: Rosewood, polished. There is a hymnal on the stand and a vase on the lid, and neither has been moved to play it.
A tuner's card is tucked in the music rest. Not mine. Somebody out here was in the trade before me, and good at it.
then: It looks like a piano that is kept, not played.

LISTEN_TO.say: …It's correct. Somebody paid to have this done properly. I may need a moment.
repeat: In tune. I keep checking. It keeps being in tune.
Nothing out of place in it anywhere. I'd like to shake whoever did it by the hand.

overrides.USE: It doesn't need me. I've never been so glad to be unnecessary.

LOOK_AT.say: A fire in a grate with a brass fender, and a coal scuttle that has been polished.
repeat: The fire irons hang in order of size. Somebody in this room runs a tight hearth.
The only fire in town that isn't also cooking something, drying something or melting something down.
A log shifting and the flame deciding where to go next.
Coal settling, warm and unhurried, like a cat.
then: It is the first one I've heard in this town that isn't complaining.

LOOK_AT.say: A proper rug, red and blue, with a border.
repeat: A border of flowers nobody in the territory has ever seen growing. It came a long way to be walked round.
There's a path worn round the edge of it. Everyone in this house walks round the rug.
then: I have wiped my boots on the step three times, and I'm still afraid of it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. A rug this good swallows footsteps whole.
repeat: Nothing. Even my boots are behaving.
Nothing. I've walked round it too, now.

overrides.PICK_UP: I would sooner pick up a sleeping bear, and with more confidence.

LOOK_AT.say: Stairs to the rooms. Forty men up there at six dollars the week, and not one of them allowed in this parlor.
repeat: A sign at the bottom: GENTLEMEN WILL REMOVE THEIR BOOTS. A row of boots under it, all removed.
The banister is polished. Nobody leans on it, because the sign says nothing about leaning and nobody wants to find out.

LISTEN_TO.say: Boots overhead, being taken off carefully.
repeat: Somebody upstairs, snoring in a respectable way.
A door closing very gently. The whole house closes doors gently.
then: The house has rules, and the rules have ears.

overrides.USE: Lodgers only, and boots off. I am neither, and I'm attached to my boots.
